transfer.stem: Which notes preserve the map’s usefulness, the speaker’s interest and the possibility of improving a task?
transfer.passage:
A class walk by the harbour
Before leaving for a harbour walk, Ms Li asked the class to check the route. Mei noticed a torn corner on their map. “It is not useless,” she said. “We can still read the route.” She also brought a spare bag for wet clothes.
At the visitor centre, the class tried a clue-finding activity. The most interesting clue was under a lid. Nearby, an old clock caught Mei’s attention. “I am interested in how old clocks work,” she said.
Some pupils thought the waiting task was boring. “A clear goal can make the task better,” Ms Li suggested. She did not promise that every task would become exciting. On the way back, the final climb was the most exciting part. From the top, the class enjoyed a wonderful view of the harbour.

options.text: A torn map must be useless; the speaker is interesting in clocks; every task has already improved.
The torn map was still readable; the speaker is interested in clocks; a clear goal can improve a boring task.
The torn map was not torn; the speaker is interested in clocks; a clear goal can improve a boring task.
The torn map was still readable; the speaker is interested in clocks; a clear goal guarantees every task will be exciting.

answer.display: The torn map was still readable; the speaker is interested in clocks; a clear goal can improve a boring task.

steps.text: 明确目标可能改善任务，不能改成已发生或保证。
steps.reason: can improve表示可能，不等于has already improved或guarantees。

distractors.reason: 反转地图用途，混淆interesting/interested，又把可能改成已发生。

把can improve扩大成每项任务都保证变得令人兴奋。

explanation.pitfall: 见到破损就判无用，把-ing和-ed混用，把可能当保证。
